Tests of the provider effects of a logistic fixed-effect fit

Source: R/test_logistic_fe.R
test.logistic_fe.Rd

Tests \(H_0: \gamma_i = \gamma_0\) for every provider (or a subset) with a chosen statistic and variance, and flags the providers above or below the null value.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'logistic_fe'
test(
  fit,
  statistic = c("exact", "score", "wald", "lr"),
  variance = c("naive", "robust", "stabilized"),
  null = "median",
  providers = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  alternative = c("two.sided", "greater", "less"),
  exact_method = c("poibin", "bootstrap"),
  score_type = c("modified", "restricted"),
  wald_variance = c("case_mix", "full"),
  n_resample = 10000,
  null_model = NULL,
  interval = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

a model fitted by fit_logistic_fe().

statistic

"exact" (default), "score", "wald" or "lr" (the likelihood-ratio statistic of \(\gamma_i\) with every other parameter held at its full-model estimate; the penalized likelihood of a Firth fit, as in ParaFLR).

variance

"naive" (default; model-based), "robust" (patient-clustered sandwich) or "stabilized" (sandwich with one within-patient correlation matrix pooled over all patients). The clustered variances need a patient column in pp_data() and are not available for the exact test.

null

the null value \(\gamma_0\): "median" (default) or "mean" (weighted by rows) of the fitted effects, or a number.

providers

optional subset of provider identifiers to report. Every provider still enters the stabilized pooling.

level

confidence level; the significance level is 1 - level.

alternative

"two.sided" (default), "greater" or "less".

exact_method

"poibin" (default; the Poisson-binomial distribution of the provider's event count, each row contributing n Bernoulli trials) or "bootstrap" (the same by simulation).

score_type

"modified" (default; \(\hat\beta\) held at the full-model estimate) or "restricted" (the other parameters re-solved under the null; naive variance only).

wald_variance

for statistic = "wald" with the naive variance: "case_mix" (default) or "full", see gamma_variance().

n_resample

number of draws for exact_method = "bootstrap".

null_model

optional null model: a pp_null object or a function of the result returning one, for instance function(t) null_model("empirical", t, n_groups = 4); the result is then passed through calibrate().

interval

for the score statistics, compute the confidence limits of \(\gamma_i\) by inverting the test (default TRUE; FALSE saves the root finding on very large data). The Wald statistics always carry their limits.

...

unused.

Value

A data frame of class pp_test with one row per tested provider: provider, estimate (\(\hat\gamma_i\)), se (Wald statistics only), null_value, statistic (a z statistic; for the exact test the normal quantile of the mid-p, for "lr" the signed root of the chi-square statistic), p, flag (1 above the null, -1 below, 0 not different, NA not testable) and, for the Wald and (with interval = TRUE) the modified score statistics, lower and upper limits for \(\gamma_i\). The score and exact statistics also carry observed (the provider's events), expected (under the null value) and variance (the variance the statistic is referred to; NA for the restricted score), which the funnel plot draws on. Attributes test (the settings) and sizes (rows and patients per provider).

Details

Row residuals \(r_j = Y_j - N_j p_j\) and variances \(v_j = N_j p_j(1 - p_j)\) are evaluated at the fitted \(\hat p_j\) for the Wald statistics and at \(p_j = \mathrm{expit}(\gamma_0 + Z_j^\top\hat\beta)\) for the score statistics. With \(U_i = \sum_{j \in i} r_j\) and \(I_i = \sum_{j \in i} v_j\):

  • naive score: \(U_i / \sqrt{I_i}\);

  • robust score: \(U_i / \sqrt{V_i}\), \(V_i = \sum_{k \in i} (\sum_{j \in k} r_j)^2\) over the provider's patients \(k\);

  • stabilized score: \(V_i\) replaced by \(\sum_{k \in i} a_k^\top \hat R a_k\) with \(a_k\) the \(\sqrt{v_j}\) of patient \(k\)'s rows and \(\hat R\) pooled over all patients by row position;

  • naive Wald: \((\hat\gamma_i - \gamma_0)/\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}}\) with the variance of gamma_variance();

  • robust and stabilized Wald: standard error \(\sqrt{V_i} / I_i\);

  • likelihood ratio: \(-2[\ell^*(\hat\gamma_{(i)}, \hat\beta) - \ell^*(\hat\gamma, \hat\beta)]\) with \(\hat\gamma_{(i)}\) the fitted effects except \(\gamma_i = \gamma_0\), and \(\ell^*\) the (penalized, for a Firth fit) log-likelihood; the other parameters are not re-estimated under the null. The statistic reported is the signed square root, so that two-sided p-values equal the chi-square tail.

The stabilized statistics take a patient's rows in their order in the data, so sort by time within patient before pp_data(). A patient with more than 5,000 rows stops the stabilized statistics.

The limits of a score statistic invert the test: with \(z_i(g)\) the statistic at the null value \(g\) (the same residuals and variance, naive, robust or stabilized, evaluated at \(g\); the correlation matrix of the stabilized variance is held at the test's null), the interval is the set of \(g\) with \(-c \le z_i(g) \le c\), so it excludes the null value exactly when the provider is flagged. A provider with no events has no finite lower limit, one with all events no finite upper limit, and a patient-clustered statistic, which is bounded by the square root of the number of events (non-events), can leave a limit infinite for a provider with very few of them. calibrate() inverts the calibrated statistic the same way.

References

Wu W, Yang Y, Kang J, He K (2022). Improving large-scale estimation and inference for profiling health care providers. Statistics in Medicine, 41(15), 2840-2853.

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 20, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_fe(pd)
test(fit, statistic = "score", variance = "robust")
